why: This is a named research dataset assembled for the brief rather than a general instructional element or education research method.
name: Shared dataset combining the Anthropic Economic Index with Census BTOS employer adoption data
product_description: A dataset used by the brief series that combines Anthropic's task-level AI exposure index with U.S. Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey employer-adoption data to inform AI-related career and technical education planning.

why: AEEGS is a named software application developed for automated scoring of extended Economics essay responses, rather than a general instructional element.

product_description: A web-based application developed by Olaoye DD et al. that uses contextual similarity to score senior-secondary Economics extended essay responses against examiner-supplied questions and marking schemes.

why: AEAIM is a review-specific, untested framework for educators' adoption of AI-enhanced PBL that combines existing theories rather than constituting a general learning theory.
This is a two-week, institution-specific course module implementation combining argumentative writing and peer feedback for one graduate student cohort, rather than a general instructional element.

name: AEQ-ES adapted to English as L2 for primary school children
product_description: A 32-item, face-supported Likert questionnaire adapted from the Achievement Emotion Questionnaire–Elementary School to measure primary pupils’ enjoyment, anxiety, and boredom when learning English as a second language.

why: The candidate is the named Academic Emotions Questionnaire, an existing assessment instrument rather than a general instructional element.
name: Academic Emotions Questionnaire (AEQ)

why: AETCOM is a named, structured medical-curriculum module that others can adopt, rather than a general instructional element.

product_description: A structured curriculum module for medical students that develops attitudes, ethics, communication skills, and sociocultural and medico-legal understanding, delivered within medical education programmes.

why: This is a single four-session continuing-education program implemented with one population in one psychiatric hospital, combining established methods rather than introducing a general reusable instructional element.

name: Anatomy Education Environment Measurement Inventory (AEEMI)
product_description: A 108-item validated Likert-scale inventory developed by Mohammadi Shabnam et al. to measure undergraduate medical students’ perceptions of the anatomy learning environment.

why: Automated Error Detection System (AEDS) is a named hardware-and-display training system used with a laparoscopic box trainer, not a reusable instructional element.
